Q: Is there an official PHP language specification? A:

An initial draft specification for the PHP language has now been announced. The introduction of the specification reads as follows:

This specification is intended to provide a complete and concise definition of the syntax and semantics of the PHP language, suitable for use by the following:

  • Implementers of a PHP compiler
  • Implementers of a test suite for the PHP language
  • Programmers writing PHP code

For now, the runtime library has been excluded, as that is documented at www.php.net. As such, all forward references to library facilities have placeholders of the form (§xx).

See also the latest version of the draft.

Q: Why does Safari not support linear color spaces in WebGPU? A:

Both srgb-linear and display-p3-linear WebGPU color spaces are now supported in Safari 27.0: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-release-notes/safari-27-release-notes#Web-API

Added srgb-linear and display-p3-linear to PredefinedColorSpace. (169340732)

Q: Calculating 2D Gaussian filter in Fragment Shader A:

One can apply 1D horizontal blur (one row at a time), followed by 1D vertical (1 column at a time). It is much faster. This comes from the fact that 2D formula exp(-x^2-y^2)=exp(-x^2)*exp(-y^2). That shows we can apply x and y blur sequentially.

Q: Why a full stop, "." and not a plus symbol, "+", for string concatenation in PHP? A:

PHP's syntax is influenced by Perl, and . is the string concatenation operator in Perl.

In a weakly typed language there are advantages to having a different string concatenation and numeric addition operators: which one you use will influence which type the language coerces the variables to.

As it happens, Perl's successor, Raku (formerly known as Perl 6) uses a tilde ~ instead of a dot . for string concatenation, because . will be used for object member access. So it seems the designers of Perl now think it was a bad choice.

Perhaps, in Perl and PHP's early, non-Object-Oriented days, it seemed like as good a choice as any. Maybe the designers of both languages never envisaged them becoming strong, Object-Oriented languages.

As for whether PHP will one day ditch its -> member access syntax for ., who knows?

Q: Write a number with two decimal places SQL Server A: 
SELECT FORMAT(104565556.785, '0.00')

Output: 104565556.79

SELECT FORMAT(104565556, '0.00')

Output: 104565556.00

Q: Dealing with 16 bits radiometric images in OpenCv A:

You can use cv2.normalize to get what you need in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the input as ANYDEPTH to preserver the 16-bit data

  • Compute the min and max values in the image

  • Use imshow with cv2.normalize to map the min and max values to 0 and 255 as 8-bit data

  • Optionally save the image similarly for viewing or labeling

Input image:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread('radiometric.png', cv2.IMREAD_ANYDEPTH)

# show the image
cv2.imshow("display version", cv2.normalize(img, None, alpha=0, beta=255, norm_type=cv2.NORM_MINMAX, dtype=cv2.CV_8U))
cv2.waitKey(0)
cv2.destroyAllWindows()


# save the image if desired
cv2.imwrite('radiometric_stretched.png', cv2.normalize(img, None, alpha=0, beta=255, norm_type=cv2.NORM_MINMAX, dtype=cv2.CV_8U))
